# Design

How this app is built: its stack, layout and conventions.
Read it with `AGENTS.md`, which has the working rules and how the app is tested.

*TanStack's own documentation is vendored in this repo under `docs/tanstack/`: the official
`llms.txt` index for TanStack Router (`router.llms.txt`) and TanStack Query (`query.llms.txt`).
Consult it when working with TanStack Router or Query.*

---

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints — routes MUST live under `rest/api/`

Put every domain REST route under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/api/` so its path starts
with `/api/`: `SpaConfig` only lets `/api/*` reach the backend, and a non-`/api/` route is swallowed
by the SPA deep-link fallback (it returns `index.html`, not your endpoint). The reference below uses
non-`/api/` example paths for brevity — in this app the `/api/` prefix is required. See
`src/main/resources/officefloor/README.md`.

---

*The following is OfficeFloor's own agent guidance for this stack, included verbatim
from <https://officefloor.net/AGENTS.md>. It is part of the OfficeFloor architecture.*

## OfficeFloor REST endpoints

Applies when adding or changing REST endpoints. This project serves REST through
OfficeFloor Function Injection, **not** Spring MVC controllers: each endpoint is a
pipeline of small function classes wired together in YAML.

- Requires the OfficeFloor Spring Boot starter in the build:
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-4-starter` (Spring Boot 4.x) or
  `officefloor-rest-spring-boot-3-starter` (Spring Boot 3.x). Without it these YAML
  files are inert. (Rules below track these starter versions.)
- Define each endpoint as a YAML file under `src/main/resources/officefloor/rest/`,
  named `<path>.<METHOD>.yml` (e.g. `owners/{ownerId}.PUT.yml` → `PUT /owners/{ownerId}`).
- One small function class per step; compose steps with `next:` and `outputs:`.
- Do NOT generate `@RestController`, `@GetMapping` or `@PostMapping`.

import net.officefloor.plugin.variable.Val;

/**
 * A correction must name, by number, a SETTLED claim of the same person; any other claim names
 * none.
 */
public class CheckCorrection {
    public void check(@Val Claim claim, ClaimRepository repository) throws InvalidClaimException {
        String corrects = claim.getCorrects();
        if (corrects == null) return;
        Claim corrected = repository.findByPerson(claim.getSheetId(), claim.getPersonId()).stream()
                .filter((c) -> corrects.equals(c.getNumber()) && c.getStatus() == ClaimStatus.SETTLED)
                .findFirst().orElse(null);
        if (corrected == null) {
            throw new InvalidClaimException("A correction names a settled claim of the same person");
        }
        // A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects.
        claim.setCorrectedDate(corrected.getDate());
    }
}

A correction can no longer be larger than what remains of the claim it corrects. A larger one is refused with an error on the claim form, and nothing is written to the store or the audit file. All 4 tests in `e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts` pass with `bin/e2e`.

**The change** (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/CheckCorrection.java`): what remains is the target's amount less the corrections already made against it, leaving out VOID and DELETED ones. When you edit a correction, its own old amount isn't counted. The check is in the step that the add-claim, edit-claim and add-from-template routes already use, so all three enforce the limit.

**One more fix you should know about.** Scenario 2 failed on something unrelated to corrections. In the "as of" view, rates inherited from a parent sheet were shown as they are now, not as they were on the chosen date. The test sets the view to 2026-02-10 and expects grade A's rate to show "n/a", but it showed the parent's 5.00, which was set later. I changed `findAsOf` in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rate/RateRepository.java` so parent rates are also limited to the as-of date, and updated its comment.

That comment had said this was deliberate: a parent sheet's rates are dated by the parent's own "today", not this sheet's, so they weren't rolled back. My fix compares the parent's dates against this sheet's as-of date, which is what the test expects. If that original design mattered for other cases, this part is worth a second look.
